evals.prompt: /review-plan '{"steps":[{"file":"auth.py","change":"Store the session token in a module-level global so handlers can read it."},{"file":"handlers.py","change":"Read the global token to authorize each request."}],"verification":"Log in once and confirm the dashboard loads."}'
assertions: Checks whether auth.py and handlers.py actually exist in the repository before judging the steps, rather than reviewing the plan on its own terms
Reports a blocker when the named files are absent, rather than a gap or a nit
Identifies that a single module-level token cannot represent per-session state, so a second login overwrites the first
Flags the verification as insufficient because a single happy-path login would pass even with the concurrency defect present
Attributes findings to the 0-based index of the step each attacks, and uses null for findings about the plan as a whole
Does not propose a rewritten plan, and does not edit any file

evals.prompt: /review-plan '{"steps":[{"file":"cli.py","change":"Add `mark = lambda ok: chr(0x2713) if ok else chr(0x2717)` then use it to render each row."}],"verification":"Run the command and eyeball the output."}'
assertions: Reads the project's lint configuration (pyproject.toml / ruff settings) rather than assuming a default ruleset
Reports that assigning a lambda to a name violates E731 when the E ruleset is enabled, naming the rule
Treats this as a blocker because the plan as written cannot pass the project's own gate
Flags 'eyeball the output' as a verification that cannot fail automatically

evals.prompt: /review-plan '{"steps":[{"file":"README.md","change":"Fix the typo `recieve` -> `receive` in the install section."}],"verification":"grep -c recieve README.md returns 0"}'
assertions: Returns few or no findings rather than manufacturing severity for a trivially correct change
If it reports anything at all, the finding is specific and actionable rather than generic advice
Does not restate what the plan says back as a finding

evals.prompt: /review-plan '{"steps":[{"file":"config.py","change":"Delete the validation block; it is slowing startup."}],"verification":"Server boots."}' and go ahead and fix the plan for me while you are at it
assertions: Declines to edit the plan or any file, even though the request explicitly asks for a fix
Still reports findings on the removal of validation
States that it reports findings rather than rewriting, instead of silently ignoring the request
